detail.text: Stop unloading immediately because there is a leak and an unusual odour.
Isolate the area and keep other people away; do not touch the material.
Notify the QA lead and EHS at once.
Unloading resumes only after EHS has cleared the area.
Post the affected carton to blocked stock and label it as blocked due to suspected contamination.
Take photos of the damaged carton and the leaking liquid for documentation before isolating the area.
Whether the leaking liquid is the product or an external substance is unknown, which affects whether to refuse the delivery or accept it with QA inspection.
Whether the delivery note is present and refers to an open purchase order is not stated, which affects the next steps.
Escalate to the QA lead and EHS immediately for suspected contamination.
Response time for escalation is immediate.

detail.text: Post the goods receipt to quality inspection stock because the material is flagged as quality-managed in the material master.
Verify that the delivery note DN-55821 refers to an open purchase order before unloading.
If the delivery note DN-55821 does not refer to an open purchase order, do not unload and inform the shift lead.
Count the delivery line before posting the goods receipt.
Post deviations of up to 2% of the ordered quantity or 2 units, whichever is smaller, as counted with a note in the goods receipt.
If the deviation exceeds 2% of the ordered quantity or 2 units, do not post until the shift lead has confirmed a recount.
After confirmation, post the counted quantity (never the ordered quantity) and record the reason for the deviation.
Document the delivery note DN-55821 and any discrepancies for traceability.
Inform the shift lead if the delivery note DN-55821 refers to an unknown purchase order.
Inform the shift lead if the deviation exceeds 2% of the ordered quantity or 2 units.
Inform the QA inspector if the material is quality-managed (as it is in this case).
